stories.title: JLL Arranges $34M Sale of Bridge Point Tacoma 210
stories.excerpt: JLL arranged the $33.9 million sale of Bridge Point Tacoma 210, a 205,413-square-foot distribution facility located at 10917 34th Ave. E in Tacoma, Washington. JLL represented the seller, Kurv Industrial, in the transaction. Completed in 2024, Bridge Point Tacoma 210 represents one of the newest industrial deliveries in Pierce County and features institutional-grade specifications designed for modern distribution operations. The JLL Capital Markets team was led by Managing Director James Ellis and Director Rachel Jones. The single-story facility offers 36-foot clear heights, 50 dock-high doors, two grade-level doors and 130-foot truck courts on 13.82 acres. The property includes 24 trailer stalls situated on nearly one acre of excess yard space and provides 130 auto parking spaces. The distribution is located five miles from Interstate 5, and nine miles from the Port of Tacoma. “Bridge Point Tacoma 210 attracted strong institutional interest due to its new construction quality and strategic location at the confluence of Tacoma’s premier submarkets,” said Ellis. The post JLL Arranges $34M Sale of Bridge Point Tacoma 210 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL sold Bridge Point Tacoma 210, 205k SF industrial, $33.9M in 2024.
New construction distribution facility, 36-ft clear heights, 50 dock doors, 13.82 acres.
Location: 5 miles I-5, 9 miles Port of Tacoma; strong institutional buyer interest.
stories.summary: JLL arranged the $33.9 million sale of Bridge Point Tacoma 210, a newly completed (2024) 205,413-square-foot industrial distribution facility in Pierce County. The single-story property features 36-foot clear heights, 50 dock-high doors, and 130-foot truck courts on 13.82 acres, positioned five miles from Interstate 5 and nine miles from the Port of Tacoma. Strong institutional interest cited the property's new-construction quality and strategic submarket confluence location.
stories.impact: Tacoma's industrial vacancy remains tight and investor appetite for newer spec warehouses near Port of Tacoma and I-5 remains strong. This signals continued absorption of new industrial supply in Pierce County; multifamily developers should monitor Tacoma-area job growth (port expansion, logistics sector) to identify residential demand tailwinds in submarkets near employment clusters.

stories.title: Investor Team Picks Up Walmart-Anchored Raleigh Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Corebridge Real Estate Investors and a fund from Armstrong Capital Development are teaming up to acquire and develop retail assets in select high-growth markets across the United States. The venture completed its inaugural acquisition with the purchase of Townridge Shopping Center, a 273,105-square-foot retail center in Raleigh. JLL Capital Markets secured the $36 million sale and $26.5 million acquisition financing of Townridge Shopping Center, which is anchored by Walmart. The center was 96 percent leased at the time of sale. Zeisler-Morgan Properties was the seller. JLL Capital Market’s Investment Sales and Advisory team, led by Tom Kolarczyk, Michael Nieder and Brian Page, represented the seller. Travis Anderson and Ward Smith secured the financing. Corebridge Real Estate Investors is the real estate equity investment management division of Corebridge Financial. CREI has an $8 billion portfolio of real estate assets under management, consisting of approximately 35 million square feet. The post Investor Team Picks Up Walmart-Anchored Raleigh Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Corebridge/Armstrong Capital acquired Townridge Shopping Center, Raleigh, $36M purchase.
273k SF Walmart-anchored retail center, 96% leased at sale; $26.5M financing secured.
High-growth retail acquisition debut for new Corebridge-Armstrong Capital joint venture.
stories.summary: Corebridge Real Estate Investors and Armstrong Capital Development completed their inaugural acquisition as a joint venture, purchasing Townridge Shopping Center in Raleigh for $36 million with $26.5 million in acquisition financing. The 273,105-square-foot retail center was anchored by Walmart and 96 percent leased at the time of sale. The venture plans to target additional retail assets in select high-growth markets.
stories.impact: Raleigh's retail fundamentals remain strong enough to attract institutional equity and leverage. The tight occupancy and successful financing signal continued health in Raleigh's retail–and by extension, its broader economic health and in-migration. Multifamily developers should view this as validation of Raleigh's growth trajectory and a sign to acquire/develop residential ahead of retail-anchored mixed-use nodes in strong Raleigh submarkets.

stories.title: Aventon Moving Ahead on 384-Unit Wesley Chapel Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Aventon paid $16.25 million for nearly 20 acres in Wesley Chapel with plans to build a 384-unit apartment community. Clearwater Bay Associates was the seller of the parcel at State Road 56 and Meadow Pointe Boulevard. Steve Lannon and Lee Arnold of Colliers represented Clearwater Bay Associates in the transaction. Eric Joseph with Coldwell Banker NRT represented the buyer.Aventon Companies broke ground on Aventon Wesley Chapel in July. The community will include one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments across six garden-style residential buildings centered around a scenic pond. Leasing is anticipated to begin in early 2028.Planned amenities include a swimming pool, 24-hour fitness center, pet spa and resident clubhouse with dedicated coworking space and social gathering areas. Clearwater Bay previously sold Aventon land near State Road 54 and Meadow Pointe Boulevard for Aventon Meadows (shown), an apartment community that opened in 2024. Clearwater Bay Associates, Inc., is a privately held Florida corporation focused on land holdings, property management and farming. The post Aventon Moving Ahead on 384-Unit Wesley Chapel Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Aventon paid $16.25M for 20 acres in Wesley Chapel, Florida; 384-unit community planned.
Broke ground July; leasing begins early 2028; garden-style, 1-3 bed units.
Amenities: pool, fitness, pet spa, coworking clubhouse; State Road 56 and Meadow Pointe.
stories.summary: Aventon Companies acquired nearly 20 acres in Wesley Chapel, Florida for $16.25 million and broke ground in July on Aventon Wesley Chapel, a 384-unit apartment community. The garden-style development across six buildings will include one-, two-, and three-bedroom units, with leasing anticipated to begin in early 2028. Planned amenities include a swimming pool, fitness center, pet spa, and a clubhouse with coworking and social spaces.
stories.impact: Wesley Chapel (Tampa metro, Pasco County) is a high-growth suburban corridor experiencing strong in-migration; Aventon's aggressive timeline (2028 delivery) and mid-market unit mix suggest confidence in rent growth and absorption. The coworking focus signals response to remote-work demand persistence in suburban Florida. This is a leading indicator of continued Tampa-area population influx and tight supply conditions favorable to new multifamily starts.

stories.title: Mexican Restaurant Santo Taco Subleases Former West Village Dig Inn Space
stories.excerpt: Santo Taco is subleasing space formerly occupied by Dig Inn in Manhattan’s West Village, Commercial Observer has learned. The Mexican food concept launched by Santiago Perez in 2025 will take over the 2,800-square-foot, street-level and below-grade space at the Steven Fuchs-owned 232 Bleecker Street at the corner of Bleecker and Carmine streets, according to ManagRE. The sublease runs until 2041. ManagRE did not disclose the asking rent in the off-market deal, but the average asking rent in nearby retail corridors in the Meatpacking District was $252 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE. Navin Bhutani of ManagRE was the sole broker in the deal, and Meerkat Development is managing the buildout of the space. Dig Inn did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Fuchs, who owns a number of properties in the West Village, could not be reached for comment. Santo Taco already has two locations at 114 Kenmare Street and 94 University Place with the new location opening next month. Perez was the CEO of Mexico City-based firm Casamata Hospitality for 10 years, managing concepts like Enrique Olvera’s Pujol as well as Cosme in the Flatiron District and Damian in Los Angeles. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Santo Taco subleased Dig Inn's 2,800 SF space, West Village, Manhattan; through 2041.
Street-level and below-grade at 232 Bleecker Street (corner Bleecker/Carmine); opens next month.
Nearby Meatpacking District avg. asking rent: $252/SF (Q2 2026); no rent disclosed.
stories.summary: Santo Taco, a Mexican restaurant concept by Santiago Perez, subleased a 2,800-square-foot space formerly occupied by Dig Inn at 232 Bleecker Street in Manhattan's West Village, with the sublease running through 2041. The street-level and below-grade space is located at the corner of Bleecker and Carmine streets and is scheduled to open next month. The transaction was an off-market deal; comparable asking rents in the nearby Meatpacking District averaged $252 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the Dig Inn closure and Santo Taco expansion reflect West Village retail churn and dining-concept consolidation; elevated comps ($252 PSF) confirm West Village remains expensive and selective for tenants, suggesting underlying residential demand remains strong but retail/amenity space is competitive and fragmented.

stories.title: Goodland Pickleball Takes 30K SF for New Indoor Clubs in Brooklyn, Queens
stories.excerpt: Indoor pickleball club operator Goodland Pickleball has secured two new club locations in New York City, Commercial Observer has learned. The long-term leases span a total of 30,100 square feet within Class A buildings in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, and Rego Park, Queens. Goodland, which secured its first indoor New York City club in Brooklyn’s Greenpoint neighborhood in 2024, reports more than 11,000 members across the city. Goodland’s Williamsburg lease, located at Rabsky Group’s 105 North 13th Street, is slated to become its new flagship location. Spanning 14,600 square feet, the club will feature four courts across two floors with 20-foot ceilings, as well as a private fifth-floor court, an outdoor terrace and a sushi bar. The Williamsburg site attracted competition from multiple pickleball operators, Hemant Chavan, founder and CEO of Goodland Pickleball, told CO. Chavan called the site “a needle in a haystack,” estimating that fewer than two dozen indoor spaces suited to pickleball’s lofty space needs exist in the city. Goodland declined to provide the asking rent, but asking retail rents along Bedford Avenue’s nearby North Eighth and North 12th streets corridor averaged $245 per square foot in the latter half of 2025, according to the Real Estate Board of New York (the most recent data available). Goodland represented itself in both lease deals, the second of which landed Goodland 15,500 square feet at RB Realty Capital’s 98-22 Queens Boulevard in Rego Park. The location will accommodate six courts, including a badminton court. Recent asking rents for Queens retail spaces averaged $42.47 per square foot, according to data from CommercialCafe. Both of Goodland’s new sites belong to Class A buildings. Chavan said Goodland is the first company in the city to operate indoor pickleball courts inside such assets. “Most indoor pickleball courts are in warehouses, and a lot of these warehouses are not prime locations,” Chavan told CO. bullets: Goodland Pickleball leased 30.1k SF across Williamsburg, Brooklyn and Rego Park, Queens.

stories.summary: Goodland Pickleball secured two long-term leases spanning 30,100 square feet in Class A buildings in Williamsburg, Brooklyn (14,600 SF flagship) and Rego Park, Queens (15,500 SF implied). The Williamsburg location at 105 North 13th Street will feature four courts across two floors with 20-foot ceilings, a private fifth-floor court, outdoor terrace, and sushi bar. Goodland reports over 11,000 members across New York City and cites extreme scarcity of suitable indoor spaces for pickleball operations.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, Goodland's rapid NYC expansion (11k members, third location) signals emerging amenity demand in Williamsburg and Rego Park; developers competing in these tight residential markets should monitor and potentially integrate specialty fitness/social amenities (pickleball, paddleball, lifestyle clubs) as differentiators in new apartment communities, especially in Williamsburg where Class A rents support premium leasing.

stories.title: National Resources Sells New York-Area Mixed-Asset Portfolio for $450M
stories.excerpt: The wait was well worth it. A more than year-long process that began last summer when National Resources CEO Lynne Ward contacted Marty Berger, co-founder of Saber-Hightower, about selling a mixture of commercial real estate assets across the New York City region as part of an estate sale produced a winning result. A joint venture between Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management acquired four National Resources properties encompassing more than 4million square feet in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut, for $450 million, Commercial Observer has learned. The acquisition, which is anchored by iPark 84, a 270-acre business park in East Fishkill, N.Y., took longer than usual to close given the amount of acreage involving three states, according to Jared Toothman, executive vice president and New York City metro market leader at Lincoln. Toothman said Berger invited him to his golf club to discuss the deal and later added Waterfall to the partnership after pitching the opportunity to investors. “We shook hands on it over a card table at a golf club and then we were off to the races,” Berger told CO. “We took a very long time to really get our hands around a portfolio to be able to extract all the pieces.” The iPark 84 property 50 miles north of Manhattan consists of a 1.8 million-square-foot campus originally developed for IBM’s flagship semiconductor manufacturing plant. It has a diverse tenant mix that includes IBM, Samsung subsidiary eMagin and agricultural company Cal-Maine, and can accommodate 1.5 million square feet of additional development The sale also features a 29-acre, mixed-use center at 761 Main Street in Norwalk, Conn., anchored by a Northwell Health medical outpatient complex, The roughly 400,000 square-foot property includes the corporate headquarters of bicycle company Cannondale, a 70,000-square-foot gym and space for approved multifamily development. The transaction also consists of Edgewater Harbor, in Edgewater, N.J
bullets: Lincoln Property/Saber-Hightower/Waterfall JV acquired National Resources portfolio, $450M.
4 properties, 4M+ SF across NY/NJ/CT; anchored by iPark 84 (270 acres, East Fishkill, NY).

stories.summary: A joint venture between Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower, and Waterfall Asset Management acquired four National Resources properties totaling more than 4 million square feet across New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut for $450 million. The acquisition is anchored by iPark 84, a 270-acre business park in East Fishkill, New York. The transaction took longer than typical due to the complexity of multi-state acreage and title consolidation.
stories.impact: This large mixed-asset portfolio sale in the NY tri-state region signals institutional appetite for non-stabilized, complex commercial real estate in secondary markets. East Fishkill is a logistics/light industrial corridor; any development or repositioning of iPark 84 or adjacent land could drive job growth and in-migration. Multifamily developers should monitor potential industrial/office-to-residential conversion opportunities or greenfield apartment sites near East Fishkill as logistics employment grows in the Hudson Valley.

stories.title: REITs Report Strong Q2 Results Even as Interest Rates Weigh on Investor Sentiment
stories.excerpt: Real estate investment trusts (REITs) performed strongly in the second quarter of 2026 — led by impressive showings in the hospitality, industrial and office sectors — but the industry as a whole remains handicapped by high interest rates and a lack of investor confidence. These are the conclusions from a new report by Hoya Capital, a private investment advisory and research company that specializes in the REIT space. Hoya Capital accumulated data from over 200 U.S. REITs and homebuilders which reported second-quarter earnings results in recent weeks, finding that 83 percent of publicly traded REITs raised full-year funds from operation (FFO) guidance — a proxy for cash flow — while just 4 percent lowered their outlooks. “Overall, REIT earnings results were surprisingly strong and delivered one of the cleanest reporting periods in recent memory, with unusually broad guidance raises, improving property-level fundamentals, and relatively few outright disappointments,” wrote Hoya Capital. The firm found that in the second quarter of 2026, national office leasing rose 16 percent year-over-year to 62.4 million square feet, buoyed by strong earnings by office giants SL Green Realty and BXP. At the same time, retail occupancy has nearly returned to pre-pandemic levels, and the industrial sector rode the data center development wave. “Higher-for-longer interest rates have been in place for a while now and REITs are finding ways to operate in a very volatile environment, whether that’s raising billions in capital or engaging in mergers and acquisitions or portfolio sales,” said David Auerbach, chief investment officer at Hoya Capital. Despite the good news, high interest rates are truly beginning to damper investor sentiment toward REITs as a whole, especially over the last month. Hoya Capital found that from July 12 through Aug. 11, the Equity REIT Index, a comprehensive measure of publicly traded REITs, declined 0.7 percent, while the S&P 500 gained nearly 4 percent. O
bullets: 83% of REITs raised 2026 FFO guidance; only 4% lowered; Q2 2026 earnings strong.
Hospitality, industrial, office sectors led performance; national office leasing rose 16% YoY.
High interest rates and weak investor sentiment remain headwinds despite strong fundamentals.
stories.summary: REITs reported strong second-quarter 2026 results across 200+ publicly traded entities, with 83 percent raising full-year FFO guidance while only 4 percent lowered outlooks. Hospitality, industrial, and office sectors led performance; national office leasing rose 16 percent year-over-year. However, elevated interest rates and low investor confidence continue to dampen overall market sentiment and capital availability.
stories.impact: Mixed signal for multifamily developers: strong operational fundamentals (occupancy, rent growth) support development thesis, but high rates and investor caution tighten construction financing and cap rates on acquisitions. Multifamily REITs not explicitly called out as leading; suggests residential is performing but not outpacing industrial/hospitality. Developers should expect continued tight leverage on deals and higher cost of capital; focus on strong submarket fundamentals and pre-leasing to de-risk financing.

stories.title: AmTrustRE Brings Financial District Office Tower to 100% Occupancy
stories.excerpt: AmTrustRE, a national real estate owner-operator, said Tuesday that 59 Maiden Ln., its 1,043,670-square-foot office tower in Manhattan’s Financial District, has reached 100% occupancy. The leasing milestone occurs with a new, 14,807-square-foot lease with Blackstone-backed ANV Group Holdings Ltd. and a 58,164-square-foot renewal from London Fischer LLP. The full occupancy comes ahead of completion of the property’s repositioning, including its facade and lobby renovations expected in 2027, and a redesigned public plaza, slated for completion later this year. “Reaching full occupancy before completing the transformation of 59 Maiden Ln. is a meaningful validation of our long-term investment strategy,“ said Jonathan Bennett, president of AmTrustRE. “By thoughtfully repositioning an exceptionally well-located asset and reinvesting in the building and tenant experience, we’ve created a workplace that drives strong leasing outcomes and competes with the best assets in the market.” ANV and AmTrustRE were both self-represented in the new lease. Bud London, Managing Partner of London Fischer, represented the firm in the renewal, while AmTrustRE was self-represented by Anne Holker, Managing Director Leasing and Acquisitions of AmTrustRE.  The post AmTrustRE Brings Financial District Office Tower to 100% Occupancy appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AmTrustRE's 59 Maiden Lane, NYC Financial District, reached 100% occupancy (1.04M SF).
Recent lease: 14.8k SF (ANV Group Holdings); renewal: 58.2k SF (London Fischer LLP).
Facade/lobby renovations, public plaza redesign underway; full repositioning completion 2027.
stories.summary: AmTrustRE announced that 59 Maiden Lane, its 1,043,670-square-foot office tower in Manhattan's Financial District, has achieved 100 percent occupancy. The milestone was achieved through a new 14,807-square-foot lease with Blackstone-backed ANV Group Holdings Ltd. and a 58,164-square-foot renewal from London Fischer LLP. The property's facade, lobby, and public plaza renovations are slated for completion in 2027.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, 100% occupancy in Manhattan's Financial District before full repositioning completion signals strong post-pandemic office recovery in Manhattan's prime submarkets. This validates continued NYC vibrancy and white-collar job retention, supporting underlying residential demand in Manhattan and inner-ring residential markets that serve FiDi workers.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges 118K-SF Price Zone Lease in Commerce
stories.excerpt: CBRE arranged a nearly 118,000-square-foot industrial lease at Harris Business Center in Commerce to Price Zone, a wholesale distributor and importer of consumer goods. The transaction allows Price Zone to consolidate operations previously spread among three separate facilities. CBRE’s Cameron Merrill and Jeff Stephens represented the landlord, DWS. The tenant was represented by John Lee of Curb Realty. “Price Zone’s primary objective was operational consolidation, and 6000 Rickenbacker Rd. provided an attractive opportunity to achieve that goal,” said Merrill. “The transaction delivered the efficiency and economics the tenant was seeking while helping ownership maximize occupancy within the business park. The result was a solution that closely aligned with each party’s long-term objectives.” The facility is located at 6000-6050 Rickenbacker Rd. and features a 24-foot clearance in the warehouse, along with 19 dock-high loading positions and three ground-level doors. It also has rail service provided by the Los Angeles Junction Railway. stories.summary: CBRE arranged a 117,900-square-foot industrial lease for Price Zone, a wholesale distributor and importer of consumer goods, at Harris Business Center in Commerce, California. The transaction consolidates Price Zone's operations from three separate facilities into a single 24-foot clearance warehouse with 19 dock-high loading doors and rail service via the Los Angeles Junction Railway. The deal delivered operational efficiency and economics for the tenant while maximizing occupancy for landlord DWS.
stories.impact: Los Angeles-area industrial market remains tight and absorbing large blocks of warehouse space; tenant consolidation reflects healthy logistics/distribution activity and supply constraints in LA metro. Multifamily developers in LA-adjacent areas should monitor continued e-commerce and distribution employment growth, particularly in Commerce, Long Beach, and Vernon submarkets, as sustained logistics demand will drive regional job growth and housing demand.

stories.title: OCVibe’s Scott Frick On Building a $5B District Around Anaheim’s Honda Center
stories.excerpt: A 100-acre master-planned development is turning the sea of parking lots surrounding Anaheim’s Honda Center into a dense mixed-use district where people can live, work and eat whether or not the Ducks are playing. Henry and Susan Samueli, owners of the National Hockey League’s Anaheim Ducks, are privately financing the large development named OCVibe. Scott Frick, senior vice president of real estate and district operations at the Samueli’s Orange County Sports & Entertainment, is managing the project, and described it as a $5 billion investment with 170,000 square feet of office space, more than 2,000 apartments, two hotels and more than 35 dining concepts. The broader plan also includes 20 acres of parks and plazas. The first major public-facing pieces are scheduled to arrive in 2027, including Katella Commons, a 50,000-square-foot market hall, along with a 5,000-capacity concert venue, and The Weave, a six-story mass-timber office building where flexible-office operator Kiln has committed to a full floor. Then the Honda Center will host indoor volleyball during the 2028 Olympics, when Frick expects roughly half a million people to pass through the arena in 11 days. Commercial Observer spoke with Frick about how the absence of outside investors changes the economics, OCVibe’s office and residential strategy, and how to keep restaurants busy when the arena goes dark. The conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Can you give an overview of where construction stands today? Scott Frick: We started construction about three years ago. We’ll be delivering phases through about 2030, 2031. The first phase was really building parking structures to free up the surface lots. Honda Center is a very typical suburban arena. It’s kind of in the middle of nowhere, surrounded by surface parking and industrial uses. Over the last eight years, we’ve assembled almost 10 different parcels to create the 100-acre footprint. bullets: OCVibe: $5B mixed-use district, 100 acres around Anaheim Honda Center; privately financed.
2,000+ apartments, 170k SF office, 2 hotels, 35+ dining; 20 acres parks/plazas.

stories.summary: Henry and Susan Samueli, owners of the NHL's Anaheim Ducks, are privately financing OCVibe, a $5 billion, 100-acre mixed-use district surrounding the Honda Center. The master plan includes over 2,000 apartments, 170,000 square feet of office space, two hotels, more than 35 dining concepts, and 20 acres of parks and plazas. First deliveries in 2027 include Katella Commons (50,000 SF market hall), a 5,000-capacity concert venue, and The Weave (six-story mass-timber office with Kiln flexible office operator).
stories.impact: OCVibe is a major supply event for Orange County residential and a major catalyst for Anaheim submarket densification and demand. The $5B private capital commitment and mixed-use scale (2,000+ units) signal confidence in Orange County's growth and affluent workforce. Multifamily developers competing in Orange County should expect significant supply influx and rental competition starting 2027; early-stage projects in surrounding Anaheim/Santa Ana submarkets should emphasize differentiation (amenities, finishes, coworking, lifestyle) and target pre-leasing to de-risk absorption risk from OCVibe ramp.
